Implement a CommonJS module exporting exactly one function named `createReadingShelf` via `module.exports = createReadingShelf`.

`createReadingShelf(initialBooks)` builds an in-memory CRUD service. `initialBooks` must be an array. Each book must have a positive safe-integer `id`, a non-empty string `title`, a positive integer `pages`, and a `status` equal to `'planned'`, `'reading'`, or `'finished'`. Duplicate IDs are invalid. Throw `TypeError` for malformed fields and `RangeError` for out-of-range or duplicate IDs. Copy the input so later external mutation cannot affect the shelf.

The returned object exposes exactly these methods:

- `list()`: returns fresh book objects sorted by ascending ID.
- `get(id)`: validates a positive safe-integer ID and returns a fresh book object or `null`.
- `add(data)`: requires valid `title`, `pages`, and `status` fields. It assigns one more than the largest ID ever assigned by this shelf, starting at 1, stores the book, and returns a fresh copy. If no safe integer ID remains, throw `RangeError` without mutation.
- `update(id, patch)`: validates the ID and a non-null, non-array patch. The patch may contain only own properties named `title`, `pages`, and `status`; an empty patch is allowed. This restriction covers every own property, including non-enumerable string properties and symbol properties, so any own symbol or any other own key is invalid. Recognized own string properties are applied even when non-enumerable, while inherited properties are ignored. Validate the entire patch before looking up or mutating the stored book. Return a fresh updated book, or `null` if the ID is absent.
- `remove(id)`: validates the ID, removes it if present, and returns whether anything was removed.

Returned and supplied objects must never alias stored books. Removing the highest ID must not allow that ID to be reused.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.

Implement an in-memory release catalog.

Export string types `ReleaseState`, `ReleaseScope`, and `ReviewerState`; a `Release` struct with fields `ID string`, `State ReleaseState`, `Scope ReleaseScope`, and `Reviewers map[string]ReviewerState`; and `Catalog` with these methods:
- `NewCatalog() *Catalog`
- `Create(id string) (Release, error)`
- `StartPublish(id string) error`
- `FinishPublish(id string, succeeded bool) error`
- `RequestRemoval(id string) error`
- `FinishRemoval(id string) error`
- `Suspend(id string) error`
- `SetScope(id string, scope ReleaseScope) error`
- `AddReviewer(id, reviewer string) error`
- `SetReviewerState(id, reviewer string, state ReviewerState) error`
- `Get(id string) (Release, bool)`

Define states `queued`, `publishing`, `ready`, `failed`, `removal-pending`, `removed`, and `suspended`; scopes `organization`, `restricted`, `partners`, and `open`; reviewer states `pending`, `approved`, and `declined`. New releases are queued and restricted. Publishing starts only from queued, and finishes only from publishing. Removal is a two-step transition from any non-removed state: `RequestRemoval` changes other non-removed states to removal-pending, and calling it while already removal-pending succeeds without changing the state. `RequestRemoval` from removed is an error. Suspension is allowed only from ready. Reviewer identifiers and release IDs must be nonblank. Reviewer updates may only select approved or declined. Duplicate releases and reviewers are errors. Invalid enum values and transitions are errors.

`Get`, `Create`, and all returned values must contain independent reviewer maps so caller mutation cannot alter catalog state. Use package `solution` and only the standard library.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
